# NEAR kit plan (xray side)

Seat: mill. Date: 2026-11-15 (CT). Refs [#1082](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082). PR [#1100](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/pull/1100).

**Status: Plan only until Blaze says start ports.**

Blaze's rule (2026-11-15 13:14 CT), quoted verbatim:

> goal is not to copy the code but get a leg up and leverage whe possible by citing the source always. but we need to go back to core near always and deep eval if the solution from the hackathon is a leg up. you and forge own this

The goal is not to copy hackathon code into xray. Cite the source always. Always go back to core NEAR first, then deeply evaluate whether the hackathon file is a leg up. Eval owners: mill + forge. A light read is not that eval.

This plan follows the working tables in [issue comment 6899635909](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899635909). For each row it lines up three points: official NEAR docs, a working file in a #1100 MIT/Apache repo, and the simplest xray kit. Mill owns the start-point file and Kit shape columns. Docs links are cited so the three points sit together; near still owns the official Docs column. Nibbler owns New (X). Pain points and package pins come from [`house/dist/nibbler/near-releases-2026-11.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/house/dist/nibbler/near-releases-2026-11.md). Gap scan (nibbler, `77581760`): [`house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md) ([#1082 comment 6899914856](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899914856)).

Scope: light read only (depth-1 clones, README + LICENSE + the named file). No code is copied into xray. Hackathon files are start points (pending eval), not a base to port from. No mainnet funds. Nothing goes to npm without Blaze GO.

Kits are builder tooling, not xray core. Each kit is self-contained under `kits/near/<kit>/` (README, install, demo, docs, start-point citation + license/NOTICE). They are not added to `src/mcps/` or the 0xray package.

## RACI (every kit)

| | Seat | Does |
|---|---|---|
| R | mill (code) and near (docs check) | mill writes the kit; near checks it against official docs |
| A | forge | accountable |
| C | nibbler | consulted (releases, X, pain points) |
| I | critic | informed; gates before any port |

Eval gate (before any port): owned by **mill + forge**. Verdict is leg up, reference only, or skip. A light read does not close it.

## Per-layer notes (docs, demo, docs vs code)

### Intents + x402 (Anyfare)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [1Click Swap API](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/about-1click-api.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — baking-bad/anyfare, MIT, `packages/topups/src/oneClick.ts` L3–5 and L544; host `packages/core/src/platform/defaults.ts` L36; x402 `packages/payments/src/x402/facilitator.ts` L4–12 and L154. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: official 1Click host and `/v0/*` paths match; no 1Click testnet so the demo is a mock; Anyfare is mainnet-oriented; x402 has no first-party NEAR docs page this pass; SDK pins (`near-api-js` v7, `@defuse-protocol/intents-sdk`) still need a current-version check. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: [1Click Swap API](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/about-1click-api.md), [making a request](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/making-a-request.md) (host `https://1click.chaindefuser.com`, `/v0/tokens`, `/v0/quote`, `/v0/status`), [confidential swaps](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/confidential-swaps) (core first for the default path), [gas keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/gas-keys). Intents index: [docs.near-intents.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near-intents.org/llms.txt). I did not find a first-party x402 page in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass; the scheme used below is [x402 NEAR exact](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_near.md).
- Confidential Intents is **on by default** in this pay kit, not a separate pack (gap scan §3; near agrees "fold into the pay kit"). Since 2026-10-27 every 1Click swap settles confidentially with no API change; `nearTxHashes` has no swap hash, only shield and unshield hashes ([changelog](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/overview)). The kit needs a status tracker on those hashes and a chain-minimum guard: origin-to-origin swaps under $1,000 USD are temporarily blocked on BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, XLayer and ADI since 2026-09-09, and under $100 on Tron since 2026-09-14 ([changelog](https://docs.near-intents.org/changelog/overview)); Base is not on either list, so prefer Base routes. The official agent skill still says "`confidentiality` values: `public` (default)" ([skill](https://github.com/near/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/near-intents/rules/api-confidential-swaps.md)) — that skill is unlicensed and **reference only**; do not base the kit on it.
- Split gas keys from meta-transactions (nearcore 2.14). A gas key cannot sign meta-tx or x402: 2.14.0 removed `DelegateV2`, and "the older `Delegate` action already rejects a gas key signer with `DelegateActionRequiresNonGasKey`" ([nearcore 2.14.0](https://github.com/near/nearcore/releases/tag/2.14.0), [gas keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/gas-keys)). x402 `exact` on NEAR is a NEP-366 signed delegate action ([scheme](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_near.md)). Use gas keys for throughput only; keep a separate non-gas function-call or full key for x402 / meta-tx (gap scan §2 and "What this means for xray kits").
- `@defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript` is **ISC** (permissive, not MIT/Apache; [repo](https://github.com/defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript)). Keep its ISC notice whenever the kit uses it. Do not vendor [near/agent-skills](https://github.com/near/agent-skills) (no license; reference only).
- Kit config: this kit's `.mcp.json` includes the three Docs MCPs (gap scan §5; core docs first: [tools for AI](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai)): `https://docs.near.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near-intents.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near.ai/mcp`.
- 5-minute demo (outline): run offline against the shipped mock 1Click/solver (pass = a dry confidential quote returns; fail = a bad asset id is refused, or a below-minimum route is guarded). Then a local x402 verify/settle against the mock, signed with the non-gas key — no real funds. Intents/1Click has no testnet (nibbler pain #1 in `near-releases-2026-11.md`). Anyfare's README claims hosted demos spend real mainnet money; the xray demo must not.
- Docs vs code: **partial match.** 1Click host and `/v0/quote` paths match the official quickstart. Anyfare splits Intents (topups) and x402 (payments facilitator) across packages; the working table names one layer. Anyfare is documented as mainnet; because 1Click has no testnet, this kit's demo is the mock path, not live 1Click. x402 itself is not a NEAR docs primitive in the official index I fetched.

### Chain Signatures (HyperNear)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [What are Chain Signatures?](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — 0xMaxyz/HyperNear, MIT, `contract/src/lib.rs` `mpc_sign` L687–711. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: the `sign` call matches the official MPC pattern, but the signed payload is Hyperliquid L1, not Base / ETH / BTC; testnet only; tests present; "intents" in this repo are EIP-712, not NEAR Intents. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: [What are Chain Signatures?](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures.md), [signing transactions](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures/implementation.md).
- 5-minute demo (outline): derive one MPC address; request one `sign` on a dummy payload via the mock path or NEAR testnet (pass = signature recovers to the derived address; fail = policy rejects an over-cap call). Do not send funds on Base in the first demo.
- Docs vs code: **disagree on the target chain.** Official docs describe signing on other chains including EVM. This contract signs Hyperliquid L1 actions, not Base / ETH / BTC. "Intents" in this repo are EIP-712 owner intents, not NEAR Intents. Testnet only; mainnet is not deployed. `sign_raw` exists only under a `spike` feature and is not in a default build.

### NEAR AI Cloud / TEE (Abalone)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [private inference](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/private-inference.md) and [GET attestation report](https://docs.near.ai/api-reference/attestation/get-attestation-report.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — amiller/abalone, MIT (keep `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), `lib/near.mjs` L115 and L120–128. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: the official `/v1/attestation/report` path matches; the file does not use `@nearai/inference-sdk`; tests present. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: [private inference](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/private-inference.md), [GET attestation report](https://docs.near.ai/api-reference/attestation/get-attestation-report.md), [inference SDK](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/inference-sdk/index.md), [OpenAI compatibility](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/guides/openai-compatibility.md). Index: [docs.near.ai/llms.txt](https://docs.near.ai/llms.txt).
- 5-minute demo (outline): `attest_model` against a fixture or mock report (pass = nonce echoes and the policy result is shown, not only "signature OK"; fail = refuse an Incognito model or a failed quote). Optional live call to `https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1/attestation/report` is not required for the cold demo. Confidential vs Incognito must stay labeled.
- Docs vs code: **match on the report path, differ on the SDK.** Abalone calls `GET /v1/attestation/report` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` directly (`lib/near.mjs`), not `@nearai/inference-sdk`. Carry `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

### OutLayer / TDX (Fulfil start file; ProvenExit registry reference)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — cuongdcdev/fullfil, MIT, `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs` L192–207 (`request_execution`). Registry reference only: erhantrk/provenexit, MIT, `contracts/near/src/lib.rs` `register_instance_tdx` L485–520. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: Fulfil calls the official OutLayer method; ProvenExit is a TDX registry and does not call OutLayer (do not treat it as a leg up for OutLayer itself); Fulfil has tests and a mainnet app, so the kit demo stays on the mock path. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md) (Rust/WASM in Intel TDX, `request_execution`). TDX attestation for *models* is on the NEAR AI Cloud side, not this page.
- 5-minute demo (outline): a local/mock `request_execution` (pass = a bound verdict returns; fail = a bad proof is refused). A registry check against a ProvenExit fixture is optional reference, not the core path. This kit leans on OutLayer, not Shade Agents (nibbler: Shade has been quiet; treat Shade as watch-only).
- Docs vs code: **the start file now matches the OutLayer docs.** Fulfil calls `request_execution`. ProvenExit verifies Intel TDX quotes *on chain* for a VPN-exit build registry and does not import OutLayer; keep it as a registry reference only. The working table still names ProvenExit as the #1100 code base; this plan re-points the kit start file to Fulfil as decided.

### 2-party key gate (Caesura)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — mitchuski/caesura, Apache-2.0 (keep `NOTICE`), `contract/src/lib.rs` `propose` L200 and `assay` L227. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: no official Caesura API; the pattern sits on function-call keys; tests present; testnet only; "intent mismatch" is a verdict reason, not NEAR Intents. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs (accounts the gate uses): [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md). Seat inference, when enabled: [private inference](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/private-inference.md) and [GET attestation report](https://docs.near.ai/api-reference/attestation/get-attestation-report.md). There is no official "Caesura" page; this is a hackathon pattern on top of function-call keys.
- 5-minute demo (outline): `npm install && npm test`, then `seats/round.mjs --task tasks/poisoned-page.json --driver stub --chain off` (pass = assayer refuses a poisoned drain; fail = proposer-only must not execute). The kit still ships the standard mock path.
- Docs vs code: **no official gate API to disagree with.** The word "intent" in the contract tests (`intent mismatch`) is a verdict reason, not NEAR Intents. johnservil/sigil was the wrong repo; this plan uses mitchuski/caesura only. Carry `NOTICE`.

### Escrow (Fulfil + Pinky)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md) and the Intents [verifier contract](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/verifier-contract/introduction.md) (no first-party escrow-kit page in `docs.near.org/llms.txt` this pass). (b) start point (pending eval) — cuongdcdev/fullfil, MIT, `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs` L3–7 and L192–207; Basssoman/pinky, MIT, `contract/src/lib.rs` `create_deal` L778 and `act` L1113. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: no official escrow kit to match; both have tests; both have mainnet deployments, so the xray demo stays on the mock path; they call Intents differently (Pinky denies `intents.near`; Fulfil holds funds in an Intents contract). (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: no first-party "escrow kit" page showed up in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass (same gap the 16:54Z scan noted). Related: Intents [verifier contract](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/verifier-contract/introduction.md) and [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md) for Fulfil's release path. Candidate official primitive for escrow / confidential multisig (core first): [NEAR Business confidential treasuries](https://docs.business.near.com/confidential-treasuries), launched 2026-10-20 ([blog](https://www.near.org/blog/introducing-near-business)).
- NEAR Business (candidate official row; eval verdict **pending**, mill + forge): each treasury is "governed by a SputnikDAO multisig contract on NEAR mainnet", funds sit in NEAR Intents on the private shard, it uses MPC threshold signing, and "NEAR Business holds no key or key share" (same docs and blog, via gap scan "Other items" #1). It is an app, not an SDK; whether it exposes an API for agents is unverified (gap scan "Unverified / open"). Caveat: funds sent to non-near.com networks by mistake "might be lost" ([funding guide](https://docs.business.near.com/guides/funding-confidential-treasuries)). Evaluate this official path before building a separate multisig pack.
- 5-minute demo (outline): create + refuse/expire against the mock 1Click/solver and a local contract path (pass = funds stay locked; fail = a denied destination or a bad proof does not pay). Pinky and Fulfil READMEs describe mainnet deployments; the xray demo uses the mock path and no mainnet funds.
- Docs vs code: **no official escrow kit to match in #1100.** Pinky *denies* withdrawals to `intents.near` (line 123); Fulfil *holds* funds as NEP-245 balances inside an `intents_contract`. They complement each other; they do not call Intents the same way. NEAR Business is the official-candidate row, not a hackathon start point.

### Scoped function-call key (nearswaps)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — nearswaps/nearswaps-agents, MIT, `packages/agent/src/keys.ts` `checkPermission` L109–118. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: matches the official access-key model; receiver is hard-coded to `nekoorders.near` and must be parameterized; tests present. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md).
- 5-minute demo (outline): `check_key` on a fixture key (pass = methods are exactly `trade, withdraw, recover_trade`; fail = a full-access key is refused). Then `preview_trade` with no send, using the mock path.
- Docs vs code: **match on the access-key model.** The allowed contract is hard-coded to `nekoorders.near`. A generic xray kit must parameterize the receiver and method list, not ship that venue as the only option. NEAR AI Cloud as a policy model is in the nearswaps README, not in `keys.ts`.

### Pre-sign MCP (Bitlens)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md) and [smart contract testing](https://docs.near.org/smart-contracts/testing/integration-test.md) (no official pre-sign primitive). (b) start point (pending eval) — NaDasai/bitlens, MIT, `mcp/server.ts` `check_transaction` L233–259. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**. Light-read inputs: no official pre-sign API; local simulator only; tests present; does not sign or send. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built.
- Official docs: none as a NEAR primitive. Closest background is [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md) and [smart contract testing](https://docs.near.org/smart-contracts/testing/integration-test.md). BitLens attacks run in a *local* simulator and only make RPC view calls.
- 5-minute demo (outline): `check_transaction` against a known demo contract (pass = allow or confirm with reasons; fail = block a dangerous method + attached deposit). Nothing is signed or sent. Ships the standard mock path.
- Docs vs code: **no official pre-sign API.** NEAR AI Cloud appears in this file only as an optional LLM for `run_custom_attack`, not as TEE attestation. The kit is the MCP tool, not a cloud attest path. Do not fold this into xray `src/mcps/`.

### Front end (gap)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) core NEAR first — [NEAR Connect](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect), [wallet login](https://docs.near.org/web3-apps/tutorials/wallet-login.md). (b) start point (pending eval) — none in the #1100 shortlist. Hasp `public/checkout.js` L20 and L105 is a 1Click widget, not this layer. (c) deep eval verdict: **pending**, leaning **skip** for a first-wave kit until a real start point exists (gap). (d) if a kit is later built, every file carries a source-citation header.
- Official docs (core first): [NEAR Connect](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect) ("Do not use NEAR Wallet Selector"). Also [wallet login](https://docs.near.org/web3-apps/tutorials/wallet-login.md), [NEAR Auth / passkeys](https://docs.near.org/web3-apps/tutorials/near-auth.md), [Social / SocialDB](https://docs.near.org/primitives/social.md). I did not find a current **web4** page in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass (unverified / possible docs move).
- Wherever wallet or connect appears, pin `@hot-labs/near-connect` **0.12.0** (npm modified 2026-10-26; gap scan §6). License is an **open question** until confirmed: npm says MIT, but the GitHub repo has no LICENSE file and GitHub reports `license: null` ([azbang/near-connect](https://github.com/azbang/near-connect)). Depend on it; do not vendor it until the license is confirmed (gap scan verdict §6).
- Docs vs code: **gap confirmed in #1100.** No shortlisted repo implements wallet selector, BOS, or web4. Official docs now say to use NEAR Connect, not Wallet Selector. Hasp and Intents Checkout are 1Click payment UIs; they belong under Intents, not this layer.

### xray vault + caps (none needed)

- Eval gate (before any port; owners: mill + forge): (a) no new NEAR doc required for this row. (b) start point (pending eval) — none; shipped xray vault and agent caps. (c) deep eval verdict: **skip** a new #1100 kit unless forge later opens a NEAR-side cap kit (Veto / Allowance would then be start points, pending eval). (d) not applicable unless that kit is opened.
- No official NEAR docs required for this row. No #1100 file. No new kit. Optional later reference: Veto `contract/src/lib.rs` `spend()` and Allowance `src/lib.rs` `pay()`, already covered in the reuse report, stay off this table unless forge opens a NEAR cap kit.

## Factory recipe

One shape for every kit above. Kits are builder tooling under `kits/near/<kit>/`, not xray core. Do not add them to `src/mcps/` or the 0xray npm package. Nothing goes to npm without Blaze GO.

| Recipe part | What every kit ships | Existing xray path / rule to follow |
|---|---|---|
| Folder layout | Self-contained `kits/near/<kit>/` with README, install, demo, docs, and the start-point citation (pending eval) plus LICENSE / NOTICE. | This is new builder tooling. Do not invent a top-level `packs/` tree and do not place kit servers under [`src/mcps/`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/tree/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/mcps). Package-face *ideas* can still follow [`docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md) (`README.md`, `package.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SKILLS.md`) inside that kit folder. A vendored kit's file set, for comparison only, is [`vendor/@0xray/repertoire/`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/tree/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/vendor/@0xray/repertoire). |
| Manifest / package face | README (what it is, when you need it), one install line, demo, docs, start-point file + license. Do not hand-bump a published version; there is no publish without Blaze GO. | [`docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md) |
| MCP tool contract | Each tool has a name, a short title, a description, and an input schema. The server lives *in the kit folder* and is started by that kit's install line. | Tool shape can follow the existing MCP style (name, title, description, input schema) used by BitLens and by xray's own servers, but the process is not registered in xray [`.mcp.json`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/.mcp.json) or `src/mcps/registry.json`. |
| Docs MCPs (kit config) | Every kit's own `.mcp.json` includes the three official Docs MCP endpoints (read-only, no API key). | Core docs first: [tools for AI](https://docs.near.org/getting-started/tools-for-ai). Endpoints from the gap scan `tools/list` check (§5): `https://docs.near.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near-intents.org/mcp`, `https://docs.near.ai/mcp`. Intents and NEAR AI also expose `submit_feedback` for stale-doc reports. This is kit-local config, not an addition to xray core `.mcp.json`. |
| Install line | One line in the kit README that adds the MCP tool from `kits/near/<kit>/`. Local checkout only. | Not `npx 0xray mcp` and not `npm publish`. No package is published until Blaze GO. |
| Mock path | Every kit ships a mock path. The 5-minute demo runs offline against a mock 1Click/solver (and any other networked solver the kit would call) so it needs no real funds. | Nibbler pain #1: Intents/1Click has no testnet (`house/dist/nibbler/near-releases-2026-11.md`). A local mock against the official 1Click OpenAPI is the default; Tidepool (MIT) is an optional later reference, not a start-file decision here. |
| Pinned SDKs | Pin `near-api-js` v7 (gap scan notes 7.5.0) and the Intents SDK `@defuse-protocol/intents-sdk`. When the kit calls 1Click, also pin `@defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript` and keep its **ISC** notice ([repo](https://github.com/defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript)). Wherever wallet or connect appears, pin `@hot-labs/near-connect` **0.12.0** ([NEAR Connect docs](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect)). Put the pins in the kit README and lockfile. | Package names from the releases file and the gap scan (`77581760`, [`near-missing-2026-11.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/house/dist/nibbler/near-missing-2026-11.md) §3, §6). NEAR Connect license is still an open question (npm MIT, no LICENSE file in [azbang/near-connect](https://github.com/azbang/near-connect)); depend, do not vendor, until confirmed. |
| Testnet / offline demo | Five minutes, pass and fail, mock path first, no mainnet funds. | Per-kit outlines above. Premise: a newb bot can run the demo from shipped artifacts only. Default RPC is a public endpoint from the official list, with an env override, as nibbler pain #5. |
| Docs page | What it is, when you need it, official NEAR URL, the #1100 start-point file (pending eval), and any docs-vs-code flag. Later: one "build an AI agent on NEAR with xray" guide that links the layer pages. | Live docs tree is `docs-site/docs/` ([`docs-site/docs/architecture/v4-foundry.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/architecture/v4-foundry.md)). Kit-local docs also live under `kits/near/<kit>/`. |
| License / NOTICE carry | MIT or Apache-2.0 only for code we would start from, plus required notices for other permitted licenses. Copy the upstream LICENSE. If a NOTICE or third-party notice file exists, ship it. | Caesura: Apache-2.0 + `NOTICE`. Abalone: MIT + `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. `@defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript` is **ISC** — keep its notice ([repo](https://github.com/defuse-protocol/one-click-sdk-typescript)). [near/agent-skills](https://github.com/near/agent-skills) has **no license**: mark it **reference only**; do not base a kit on it or vendor it (gap scan §4). `@hot-labs/near-connect` is MIT on npm but has no LICENSE file in the repo: **open question** until confirmed; depend, do not vendor (gap scan §6). near-sandbox is GPL and is for local testing only — do not pack it ([sandbox testing](https://docs.near.org/smart-contracts/testing/integration-test.md)). |
| Eval gate (before any port) | Always go back to core NEAR first, then evaluate the hackathon start point. Do not copy it in. Cite the source always. Owners: **mill + forge**. | (a) official core NEAR doc URL. (b) hackathon file cited: repo, path, lines, license. (c) deep eval verdict: **leg up** / **reference only** / **skip**, with the reason (matches official API? current SDK version? tests? mainnet/testnet?). A light read is not this verdict. (d) every kit file carries a source-citation header when built (official doc + start-point repo/path/lines/license + verdict). |
| Critic gate before any port | No #1100 code is copied, and no kit is ported, until Blaze says start ports, the mill+forge eval gate has a verdict, forge's RACI holds, and critic passes. | Gate skill: [`grok-bot/skills/ship-ready-mill-gate/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/grok-bot/skills/ship-ready-mill-gate/SKILL.md). Foundry gate script: [`scripts/foundry/release-gate.mjs`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry/release-gate.mjs). |
| Cold test of the packed tarball | Pack the kit folder and assert it contains the runtime files (MCP entry, docs, LICENSE / NOTICE, mock path). Do not `npm publish`. | Pattern to copy later: [`scripts/foundry/assert-packed-dist-cli.mjs`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry/assert-packed-dist-cli.mjs) and [`src/__tests__/unit/wear-pack-file-list.test.ts`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/__tests__/unit/wear-pack-file-list.test.ts). Run that style of assert *inside the kit*, not as a publish of `0xray`. |

Build order from the premise, still valid: Intents + x402 first, then Chain Signatures (Base path), then NEAR AI TEE, then the Caesura two-party gate. Escrow, trading key, and pre-sign can follow. Front end stays docs-only until a start point exists and passes eval. Spending caps stay on the shipped xray vault.
